mood.p: Maandag 7 september wordt de warmste dag van de week. Na een nacht van 10 tot 16 graden schijnt de zon volop en blijft het droog, met maxima van 24 graden in het westen tot plaatselijk 29 in het zuidoosten. In de middag draait de wind naar het westen en aan de zuidwestkust wordt het met windkracht 5 tot 6 flink winderig; in de avond kan lokaal een bui vallen. Dinsdag regent het bij 20 graden en woensdag, de dag van de landelijke ov-staking, is het wisselvallig met 18 graden en veel wind. De stemming is bedrukt. Over de grens won de AfD zondag met ruim 44 procent in Saksen-Anhalt, in de Golf escaleert de tankeroorlog tussen de VS en Iran en de olieprijs nadert 97 dollar. In Overasselt werd een herdenking voor beveiliger Berry Leenders om veiligheidsredenen afgelast en acht dagen voor Prinsjesdag zoekt het kabinet-Jetten nog steun voor de begroting. Lichtpuntjes: de Amsterdam City Swim haalde ruim 3 miljoen euro op voor ALS-onderzoek en Telstar-keeper Ronald Koeman jr. scoorde twee keer.

global.h3: Iran to declare restricted zone beyond Hormuz as tanker war escalates
global.summary: Tehran said on Sunday 6 September it will announce a restricted zone starting at the line of the US naval blockade, a day after Washington struck three Iranian tankers and Iran hit vessels it called unauthorised.
body: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told state media on Sunday 6 September that a restricted zone will be declared within days. It would begin at the line of the US Navy blockade and cover parts of the Gulf, and any ship entering it would be added to Iran's sanctions list. Maps of approved Hormuz lanes have been agreed with Oman.

The announcement followed the sharpest exchange at sea in weeks. US Central Command said it disabled two Iranian tankers and destroyed a third on Saturday after the Revolutionary Guard fired missiles at an American carrier and destroyer. Iran's navy said it hit three tankers and three US-linked vessels in return. Kpler data show only about 13 ships a day transiting the strait.

global.h3: Trump says US may hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain 'very soon'
global.summary: Speaking in the Oval Office on Saturday 5 September, the president said intelligence is tracking every movement at the fortified site near Natanz and that any suspicious activity would be met with a hard strike.
body: President Donald Trump said on Saturday 5 September that the United States could strike Pickaxe Mountain, the deeply buried tunnel complex beside Iran's damaged Natanz enrichment plant, very soon. He said American intelligence knows who is moving at the site and the US will hit hard if anything goes wrong. Israeli intelligence reportedly believes Iran has moved thousands of centrifuges into the tunnels.

The warning came hours before US missiles struck an Iranian tanker off Kharg Island and revived a threat Trump first made in July. Analysts told Al Jazeera the timing reflects frustration that the June memorandum has produced no settlement, plus midterm pressure as fuel prices climb. Iranian officials said the site is protected and any new attack would end the diplomatic track.

global.h3: Witkoff and Kushner call Kyiv talks 'substantive' after meeting Putin
global.summary: The US envoys made their first visit to Ukraine on Sunday 6 September, meeting Zelensky twice and then European security advisers, one day after three hours with Putin in the Kremlin.
body: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday 6 September after flying from Moscow to Rzeszow in Poland and continuing overland. It was their first trip to Ukraine and the highest-level American visit since Trump returned to office. They met President Volodymyr Zelensky twice, then held a third session with the national security advisers of Britain, France and Germany.

Zelensky said the talks covered security and economic guarantees, air defence missile deliveries and a support package for the coming winter. A participant told Axios the envoys want a refreshed peace proposal and a breakthrough before the cold months. Kushner relayed greetings from Trump and spoke of a durable peace. Analysts in Kyiv cautioned the visit may prove more ceremonial than decisive.

global.h3: Kremlin calls Moscow talks frank but insists on 'root causes' and joint projects
global.summary: After Saturday's three-hour meeting, Putin's aide Yuri Ushakov said a series of peace ideas was formulated, while stressing that Russia is confident of taking the rest of eastern Ukraine.
body: Vladimir Putin received Witkoff and Kushner at the Kremlin on Saturday 5 September, telling them the situation was not simple. Foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov called the talks substantive, frank and constructive and said a series of settlement ideas had been drawn up. He repeated that the root causes of the conflict must be resolved and that Moscow expects to reach its military goals.

Ushakov added that economic issues and potentially large joint projects between Russia and America were discussed in detail. A White House official said next steps would be announced within weeks and that Trump and Putin would stay in contact. Russian commentators said the Kremlin was less pessimistic than after previous visits because it believes it holds the battlefield advantage.

global.h3: Capitals spared under three-day truce, but strikes elsewhere kill civilians
global.summary: Russia and Ukraine kept their promise not to hit Kyiv or Moscow during the envoys' visit, yet drones and missiles struck other regions overnight into Sunday, killing at least one person on each side.
body: Under the limited truce agreed for the American mission, the Kremlin ordered no strikes on Kyiv from midnight on Saturday and Zelensky said Ukraine would spare Moscow through Monday. Both capitals were quiet, but the wider air war continued. Ukraine's emergency service said Russian attacks killed one person and injured at least ten overnight into Sunday 6 September, including a 74-year-old man in Zaporizhzhia.

Ukraine's air force reported intercepting 82 of 108 drones and six missiles. In Belgorod, a Ukrainian drone struck a vehicle and killed a man, while Russia's defence ministry claimed 258 Ukrainian drones were downed over 14 regions, Crimea and the Black and Azov seas. Saturday's Russian strikes had killed at least seven people before the pause along the 1,250 kilometre front.

global.h3: Israeli strikes kill four in south Lebanon after Hezbollah drone attack
global.summary: Lebanon's health ministry said two people died in Nabatieh al-Fawqa and two women in Arab Salim on Sunday 6 September, after Hezbollah sent explosive drones at Israeli troops in the border zone.
body: Israeli aircraft struck several sites in southern Lebanon on Sunday morning 6 September, killing four people and wounding around twenty, Lebanese authorities said. The military said the raids answered two explosive-laden drones launched by Hezbollah at soldiers near the Ali Taher ridge. Before one strike, the army ordered residents of Arab Salim to move at least 300 metres from a building it said Hezbollah was using.

Targets included the disused Ghandour hospital in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, which Israel said had become a command post for artillery and surveillance units, and weapons depots. It was the second such exchange in three days after Friday's strikes killed three people. Chief of staff Eyal Zamir called the period ahead of the Jewish holidays tense and volatile, underlining how fragile the border arrangement remains.

global.h3: Houthi missile kills four civilians near Taiz as 1,800 families flee
global.summary: A strike on the crowded Heijah al-Abd road south of Taiz on Saturday 5 September killed at least four people and injured nine, amid renewed fighting on the Taiz and Hodeidah fronts.
body: At least four civilians were killed and nine wounded on Saturday 5 September when a Houthi missile hit a gathering on the strategic Heijah al-Abd road south of Taiz city in southwestern Yemen. The road is a lifeline for the government-held city, under partial Houthi siege for years. Local officials said the victims were travellers and traders. The Iran-aligned group did not immediately comment.

The attack came amid the heaviest ground fighting in months along the Taiz and Hodeidah front lines, where Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis contest routes to the Red Sea coast. The UN humanitarian office said nearly 1,800 families fled their homes in under 48 hours. Aid agencies warn the renewed war, layered on the Hormuz conflict, is pushing Yemen's food and health systems toward collapse.

global.h3: Six-year-old among two killed in Gaza City strike on first day of school
global.summary: Palestinian medics said an Israeli strike on a vehicle near Al-Shati on Sunday 6 September killed a girl travelling with her father, while seven others were wounded in the refugee camp.
body: Two Palestinians, including a six-year-old girl, were killed on Sunday 6 September when an Israeli strike hit a vehicle in Gaza City, Palestinian medical sources said. The girl was reportedly travelling with her father near the Al-Shati refugee camp on what should have been the first day of school. Seven more people were wounded in two separate strikes in the camp.

The deaths show how thin the Gaza ceasefire has become as Israel heads toward a general election on 27 October. UN teams collected hundreds of pallets of supplies from the Kerem Shalom crossing over the weekend, but agencies say access remains erratic. Eight Muslim-majority states condemned Israeli ministers' emigration proposals, and US envoy Jared Kushner said election politics was making Israeli decisions on Gaza irrational.

global.h3: AfD wins Saxony-Anhalt with 44 percent, first far-right state victory
global.summary: Exit polls on Sunday 6 September put the AfD far ahead of Merz's CDU on 18.5 percent, though the party appears to fall just short of the absolute majority it needs to govern alone.
body: Alternative for Germany scored a historic result in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday 6 September, taking around 44 percent of the vote according to exit polls for ARD and ZDF. That is more than double its 2021 share and about two and a half times the 18.5 percent of the Christian Democrats, who have governed the eastern state for 24 years. The Left Party came third on roughly 9 percent.

Lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund, 35, told ARD his party had written history and thanked the unpopular Chancellor Friedrich Merz for campaigning so well for the AfD. Because all other parties refuse to work with the AfD, it needs an outright majority of seats to form the first far-right state government since 1945, and exit polls suggest it is marginally short.

global.h3: Eight Muslim-majority states condemn Israeli plans to push Gazans out
global.summary: Saudi Arabia, Jordan, the UAE, Turkey, Qatar, Egypt, Indonesia and Pakistan issued a joint statement on Sunday 6 September calling the Katz and Ben Gvir proposals a flagrant breach of international law.
body: The foreign ministers of eight Muslim-majority countries jointly condemned remarks by Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz and National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir on Sunday 6 September. In an Arabic-language statement, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Turkey, Qatar, Egypt, Indonesia and Pakistan said the proposals amounted to mechanisms for forcibly expelling Palestinians and a direct threat to their legitimate rights.

Ben Gvir presented a plan on Thursday to remove most of Gaza's 2.3 million residents through what he termed voluntary emigration, including a dedicated ministry, if the coalition survives the October election. Katz said Israel was ready to facilitate departures by land, sea and air but conceded no country would take people on that scale. Several signatories are Washington's partners in the ceasefire framework, making the rebuke awkward.

global.h3: Iran's rial hits record low as Pezeshkian pleads for unity under US squeeze
global.summary: The currency passed 2.25 million to the dollar when markets opened on Saturday 5 September, and the president warned that Iranians are on the edge as Washington's sanctions campaign bites.
body: Iran's rial fell to a record low of more than 2.25 million to the US dollar on Saturday 5 September. The slide follows the US Treasury's announcement last month of what it called an Economic D-Day, the toughest sanctions package in American history, aimed at every revenue stream sustaining the government and Revolutionary Guard. The naval blockade has already strangled oil exports through Kharg Island.

President Masoud Pezeshkian insisted officials and citizens would stand together and that national cohesion could defeat attempts to sow discord. But he acknowledged people are on the edge and another shock could push them over, so he will avoid abrupt policy changes. The government will still double the price of one tier of subsidised petrol. Analysts told Al Jazeera Iran aims to break the siege.

global.h3: Oil opens near 97 dollars as Gulf strikes and Hormuz zone rattle markets
global.summary: Brent rose as much as 0.8 percent at the Asian open on Monday 7 September after the weekend's tanker attacks and Iran's plan for a restricted zone, while polls show US voters souring on the war.
body: Brent crude climbed toward 97 dollars a barrel and West Texas Intermediate traded around 92 dollars when Asian markets opened on Monday 7 September, according to Bloomberg. Traders were reacting to US strikes on three Iranian tankers, Iran's attacks on shipping and Tehran's restricted zone beyond Hormuz. Brent closed Friday at 96.28 dollars, up from about 70 dollars before the war began on 28 February.

The surge is feeding into American politics two months before the midterms. US diesel hit a record average of 5.85 dollars a gallon on Friday, and a late-August Reuters/Ipsos poll found 63 percent of Americans oppose the war against 31 percent in favour, with Trump's approval at 33 percent. Kpler tracking shows only a handful of vessels transiting the strait daily.

global.h3: Canada's dollar-for-dollar tariffs on US goods take effect on Tuesday
global.summary: Levies of 15 to 50 percent on roughly 20 billion dollars of American products, from steel and dairy to dishwashers and ice skates, start on 8 September with no sign of talks resuming.
body: Canada's retaliatory tariffs against the United States come into force on Tuesday 8 September, two weeks after Prime Minister Mark Carney announced them in response to Washington's 50 percent duties on Canadian goods. The measures cover about 20 billion dollars of US exports at rates between 15 and 50 percent, targeting steel, dairy, appliances, farm machinery, pulp and paper and electronics.

The two sides had appeared close to a deal in August before talks collapsed over conditions Ottawa called unacceptable, prompting Carney to say Canada was at war after being attacked. Trump replied that Canada wanted the benefits of statehood without joining. Trade minister Dominic LeBlanc welcomed a US shift on cultural rules, but no new negotiating round is scheduled. Business groups say the counter-tariffs enjoy broad public support.

global.h3: Nepal flood toll reaches 1,384 as Kathmandu files climate compensation claim
global.summary: Twelve days after the glacial collapse, 1,341 bodies have been recovered in Nepal and nearly 5,000 people are missing, and the government has asked the UN loss and damage fund to help pay for the disaster.
body: Rescuers in Nepal and Tibet were still searching for more than 5,500 missing people on Sunday 6 September, twelve days after a glacial collapse sent floods down the Trishuli valley. Nepal's disaster agency said 1,341 bodies had been retrieved and about 4,996 people remained unaccounted for, including hundreds of foreigners. In Tibet the toll rose to 43 dead with 519 missing.

Nepal has formally asked the UN-backed Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage to cover part of the cost. Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said big emitters have a historical responsibility to compensate vulnerable nations. The UN has appealed for 50 million dollars to help 84,000 people. The fund holds only about 631 million of 822 million dollars pledged.

global.h3: UN: wildfires push north as 600,000 hectares burn in EU this year
global.summary: UN agencies say historically cool and wet countries from Britain to Scandinavia must now prepare for fire seasons, after peat fires in the Scottish Cairngorms resisted containment this summer.
body: More than 600,000 hectares have burned inside the European Union in the first eight months of 2026, according to the European Forest Fire Information System. That is below the 2025 record but more than double the twenty-year average of roughly 280,000 hectares. UN agencies are helping governments adapt as the risk spreads from France and Spain into the United Kingdom and Scandinavia.

WHO Europe pointed to a mid-July wildfire in Scotland's Cairngorms that burned into the dry peat layer. Most fires are started by people, but their speed and intensity are shaped by warmer, drier conditions linked to climate change. The agencies want northern countries to build smoke-health warnings and firefighting capacity. The Netherlands recorded its hottest summer ever this year.

netherlands.h3: Cabinet to detain asylum seekers for transfer to first EU country of entry
netherlands.summary: The Ministry of Asylum and Migration wants a pilot placing Dublin claimants in immigration detention to make handovers stick, NRC reported and COA confirmed on Sunday 6 September.
body: The Jetten cabinet wants far more asylum seekers sent back to the European country where they first applied for protection, and plans to detain some of them. NRC reported that the Ministry of Asylum and Migration will start a pilot placing people who fall under the Dublin Regulation in immigration detention while their handover is arranged. COA confirmed the pilot on Sunday 6 September.

NRC called it the first far-reaching asylum measure of this cabinet aimed at people with little chance of a Dutch residence permit. Under Dublin rules the first EU country of arrival handles the claim, but transfers often fail because applicants disappear. New European rules allow up to three years for a transfer. COA shelters are running above 100 percent capacity.

netherlands.h3: PBL: nitrogen plan means 30 percent fewer cows, grid operators cheer
netherlands.summary: The environmental agency says the cabinet's package takes large steps but leaves most nature areas overloaded in 2035, while Netbeheer Nederland urges a fast exemption for energy projects.
body: The Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency PBL says the cabinet's nitrogen package is very ambitious, but will not release the country from the nitrogen lock in one go. Director Marko Hekkert estimated the plans would leave the Netherlands with about 30 percent fewer cows. The package targets a 42 to 46 percent cut in farm emissions by 2035 and 50 percent from industry and traffic.

Even if all measures are delivered, only 14 of 120 nitrogen-sensitive nature areas would no longer be overloaded in 2035 and a further 5 to 10 percent cut in livestock rights would be needed. Netbeheer Nederland said nature restoration and economic development can go together and pressed the cabinet to deliver a promised exemption for energy infrastructure quickly.

netherlands.h3: FNV shifts strike hours as Wednesday's 24-hour transport shutdown nears
netherlands.summary: NS trains, regional buses and city transport stop from 02:00 on 9 September; the union says 70 percent of the planned social security cuts remain, so the action against the cabinet goes ahead.
body: Wednesday's nationwide public transport strike is confirmed. After a safety meeting on 3 September, FNV agreed to an NS request to run the train strike from 02:00 on Wednesday 9 September until 02:00 on Thursday. GVB, RET and HTM stop from the first to the last service. Only the Airport Sprinter between Amsterdam Central, Schiphol and Hoofddorp will run.

The union says the leaked budget shows the cabinet is postponing rather than scrapping cuts to unemployment benefit and WIA disability payments, with about 70 percent of the savings still planned. FNV stresses the action targets The Hague, not NS or travellers, and warns September will bring strikes in ports, government, healthcare and the metal sector.

netherlands.h3: Eight days to Prinsjesdag and the cabinet still lacks a budget majority
netherlands.summary: Jetten and Heinen say they wrote a budget for ten parties, but Pro leader Klaver says he has heard nothing since late August and the SGP calls the sequence highly uncertain.
body: With the King's Speech on Tuesday 15 September, the minority coalition of D66, VVD and CDA is entering its final week. Finance Minister Eelco Heinen said the budget was drafted for ten parties rather than three, and Prime Minister Rob Jetten rates the chances of majority support as quite good. Leaked details suggest most social security cuts are reversed or delayed.

The opposition remains unconvinced. Pro leader Jesse Klaver said he had not heard from Jetten since their last meeting and feared the coalition had again postponed the problem. SGP leader Chris Stoffer called it an unhappy order of events. An Ipsos I&O poll on Saturday put dissatisfaction with the cabinet at a record 70 percent.

netherlands.h3: Industry-backed study says no sugar tax design delivers 900 million a year
netherlands.summary: PwC research commissioned by food lobby FNLI, reported on Sunday 6 September, finds the cabinet's revenue goal and health goal pull in opposite directions and would boost cross-border shopping.
body: None of the sugar tax options the cabinet is weighing can reliably raise money, be enforced and clearly improve health, according to a PwC study commissioned by the food industry association FNLI. The cabinet wants a broad sugar levy to raise about 900 million euros a year from 2030. PwC found a tax that really cuts sugar intake erodes its own revenue.

The consultants assessed several designs on feasibility, enforcement and fraud risk and concluded none passed the health, revenue and legal tests. A Dutch levy would also widen the price gap with Belgium and Germany, where four in ten Dutch people already buy cheaper soft drinks. Health advocates note that half of Dutch children drink 16.5 glasses of sugary drinks a week.

netherlands.h3: Omtzigt calls Malta acquittal in Caruana Galizia murder 'extremely painful'
netherlands.summary: The former MP, who investigated the case for the Council of Europe, said on Sunday 6 September that apparently no one is guilty of ordering the 2017 car bomb killing of the journalist.
body: Pieter Omtzigt reacted with dismay to the acquittal of Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech, whom a jury on Wednesday cleared of masterminding the 2017 car bomb murder of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Writing on X, the former Dutch lawmaker said it was extremely painful and that apparently no one is guilty of ordering the killing.

Fenech was indicted in 2021 on charges of complicity and conspiracy after a middleman turned state witness; the three men who planted the bomb have already been convicted. The verdict angered Caruana Galizia's family and drew condemnation from Reporters Without Borders, while Malta's government appealed for calm amid protests. For Omtzigt, the case tests whether EU states uphold the rule of law.

netherlands.h3: Rabobank lifts growth forecast to 1.3 percent but warns of Hormuz stalemate
netherlands.summary: The bank now expects 1.3 percent growth this year and 1.1 percent next, driven by household and government spending, with inflation rising to 3.4 percent in 2027 as energy stays expensive.
body: Rabobank raised its outlook for the Dutch economy on Sunday 6 September, forecasting growth of 1.3 percent in 2026 and 1.1 percent in 2027. The upgrade rests on consumers, whose wages are still rising faster than prices, and on government spending on ageing and defence. Inflation is expected to climb from 2.8 percent this year to 3.4 percent next year.

The economists stress that uncertainty is greater than usual. Their baseline assumes a lasting stalemate between the United States and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz, keeping energy prices high. Household spending is expected to slow in 2027 and business investment to stall. The bank also notes the Jetten cabinet lacks a majority, so extra public spending is not guaranteed.

netherlands.h3: Ten million Dutch live in homes that overheat, and new builds follow 1996 rules
netherlands.summary: Experts told NU.nl that housing standards still assume the climate of 1996 and 2015, even though more than 3,500 people died during June's heat and 100,000 homes a year are being built.
body: Dutch homes were designed for a cooler climate and are becoming dangerously hot in summer, experts warned in a report on Sunday 6 September. More than 3,500 people died in the Netherlands during the extreme heat of June, and every KNMI scenario shows warmer summers. Yet homes built since 2021 meet overheating standards based on the climate of 1996 and 2015.

Jeroen Kluck said houses designed today will still stand in 2050 and should be calculated for that climate. With the government aiming to build 100,000 homes a year, experts fear a generation of dwellings that trap heat. Investico found nearly 10 million residents, including 2 million over 65, live in homes that can get too hot. The housing ministry says the standards are under review.

netherlands.h3: Arbo Unie declares start of 'absence season' with 69 percent more sick reports
netherlands.summary: Analysis of 2020 to 2025 data shows September sick leave runs 69 percent above August, the occupational health provider said on Sunday 6 September, with stress driving the long-term cases.
body: Occupational health provider Arbo Unie expects a sharp rise in sick leave from this week. Based on reports from 2020 to 2025, the number of employees calling in sick in September is on average 69 percent higher than in August. Occupational physician Corne Roelen said workplaces get busier and the flu season begins, not that people have lost the will to work.

Almost three quarters of September absences last year were shorter than a week. A relatively larger share, however, develops into long-term absence, and in those cases mental health problems such as stress are the leading cause. Absence peaks in January, February and March. The findings arrive as employers prepare for Wednesday's transport strike over WIA disability benefit cuts.

netherlands.h3: Overasselt: 35th suspect held, memorial for slain guard cancelled over safety
netherlands.summary: Police arrested a 26-year-old Belgian on Sunday 6 September, searched the village for weapons and bullets, and a Nijmegen student association scrapped its tribute to Berry Leenders.
body: Police announced on Sunday 6 September that a 35th suspect, a 26-year-old man from Belgium, has been arrested over the shooting in Overasselt on 1 September that killed security guard Berry Leenders, 51, and wounded two police officers. Of the 34 people detained earlier, 32 were remanded in custody, among them 16 French nationals including two teenagers, 11 Dutch adults and suspects from Belgium, Libya, Ukraine and Algeria.

The violence appears linked to a dispute over almost 1,900 kilograms of cocaine that a masked group, in a video circulating online, accused local man Jan G. Junior of stealing. Residents told Omroep Gelderland that others in the area have received threats. A memorial for Leenders planned by Nijmegen student association Carolus Magnus was cancelled for unspecified safety reasons.

netherlands.h3: Record 3,300 swimmers raise over 3 million euros for ALS in Amsterdam canals
netherlands.summary: The Amsterdam City Swim on Sunday 6 September brought in 3,007,246 euros, a record, with twelve people living with ALS among those who covered the two kilometres from the Keizersgracht to the Marineterrein.
body: More than 3,300 people jumped into the Amsterdam canals on Sunday 6 September for the Amsterdam City Swim, the largest field in the event's history. The day opened with a 750 metre Short and Junior Swim before presenter Ruben Nicolai started the main two kilometre event. Twelve participants with ALS took part. Organisers announced a record total of 3,007,246 euros.

Every euro goes to research into ALS and the related diseases PLS and PSMA through Stichting ALS Nederland. Chair Daan Vos said he had seen at close range how merciless the disease is and that each euro brings an effective treatment closer. The event began in 2011; the final figure will be announced on 1 October.

netherlands.h3: Utrecht fans force abandonment; Koeman Jr first keeper to score twice
netherlands.summary: Fireworks and cups halted FC Utrecht v Go Ahead Eagles at 3-1 on Saturday 5 September, while Telstar goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr converted two penalties in a 2-2 draw with Cambuur on Sunday.
body: Referee Martin van den Kerkhof abandoned FC Utrecht's home match against Go Ahead Eagles on Saturday 5 September after supporters behind the goal twice disrupted play. With the visitors 3-0 up, fireworks halted the game for twenty minutes. At 3-1, a shower of plastic cups ended it. The final 25 minutes will be played behind closed doors on Tuesday.

Sunday brought a happier first in IJmuiden, where Telstar goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr became the first keeper to score twice in an Eredivisie match, converting two penalties, for a 2-2 draw with Cambuur. PSV won the season's first topper 3-1 at Ajax, Feyenoord beat NEC 3-1 and Max Verstappen finished third at Monza behind both Mercedes drivers.

netherlands.h3: Three Dutch men arrested at cocaine cutting-agent lab just over Belgian border
netherlands.summary: Dutch and Belgian police raided a warehouse in Pelt on Thursday and found a working lab processing procaine, with a linked search in Valkenswaard turning up gas masks and a large tank.
body: Three Dutch nationals have been arrested after Belgian and Dutch officers uncovered a drug laboratory in a warehouse in Pelt, in Belgian Limburg just across the border from Noord-Brabant, NL Times reported on Sunday 6 September citing HLN. The suspects are a 41-year-old from Valkenswaard, a 41-year-old registered in Pelt and a 45-year-old from Eindhoven. Police ordered the men out at about 7 a.m. on Thursday.

Inside, investigators found an operational lab chemically processing procaine, a substance used as a cutting agent to bulk up cocaine before sale. A follow-up raid in Valkenswaard yielded gas masks and a large processing tank. Neighbours told HLN the building had long seemed suspicious, occupied only sporadically by people who then vanished for weeks.
